newsitem.title: BELGIUM: FOCUS - MAYSTADT, KREDIETBANK TARGET OF TAX PROBE.
newsitem.headline: FOCUS - MAYSTADT, KREDIETBANK TARGET OF TAX PROBE.

text.p: Belgian judicial police on Monday searched the offices of Finance Minister Philippe Maystadt in a probe into suspected tax fraud by Belgian banks and questioned staff of leading Belgian bank Kredietbank, officials said.

"The offices of the finance ministry cabinet and of the administration have been searched by the judicial police. This was in the framework of a probe into tax practices by certain banks," a finance ministry spokesman told Reuters.
He added Maystadt's personal office had not been searched.
RTL television said some cabinet officials' private residences had also been searched.
Maystadt said he did not know the purpose of the search.
"I have to find out what this is about. I am relaxed," Maystadt told RTL.
In recent weeks, Maystadt has been dogged by reports in the Belgian press saying that he had been lenient to certain banks with regard to tax cases.
The judicial police also questioned staff members of Kredietbank NV , one of Belgium's top four banks, in a tax fraud probe.

"The judicial police is at this moment questioning staff members of our fiscal department. We do not know what this is about, it may have something to do with a bourse operations tax case or with our Luxembourg sister bank Kredietbank Luxembourg," a spokeswoman for the bank told Reuters.
Belgian media have reported that Maystadt had intervened with the tax administration in favour of Kredietbank, but it was not immediately clear whether the court's two actions on Monday were related.
Maystadt has has denied any wrongdoing with regard to his alleged intervention in favour of Kredietbank.
Kredietbank has been under fire in recent weeks in Belgian media over allegations of tax evasion.
One case involves the so-called flat-rate tax on income from foreign investments.

In the late eighties, coupons on bonds from certain countries gave right to a flat-rate tax break, even if no taxes had been paid abroad. Belgian media have said banks also passed on benefits from this tax loophole to their corporate clients. The Belgian tax authorities are now allegedly reclaiming bourse tax on the securities sold in this framework.
Kredietbank Luxembourg, Kredietbank's sister bank, has been the object of an investigation into tax avoidance since last year.

Kredietbank shares topped the volume chart on the Brussels bourse. By 1400 GMT the share stood 1.3 percent lower at 11,625 francs with a hefty 12,887 shares traded. The raid on Maystadt's office also weighed on the Belgian franc, which continued its recent easing. It was quoted 20.6315/25 to the mark, from 20.6293/03 on Friday.
